We got search results, first entry reaction_id 1118219 with retro_smarts_template: '[c:6]-[N;H0;D3;+0:5]1-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[#7:7]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[CH2;D2;+0:4]-1>>Cl-[c;H0;D3;+0:1]1:[cH;D2;+0:2]:c:c:[cH;D2;+0:3]:[cH;D2;+0:4]:1.[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]'

This is a retro template: product (our target) is the heterocycle attached to aromatic ring? Actually product side is left side of >>? In retro, left side is product? The retro_smarts_template shows product side (left) is [c:6]-[N...] (the heterocycle) and reactants (right) are Cl-aryl and NH2-aryl. So applying this template to our target should give precursors: an aryl chloride and an aryl amine (NH2 attached to aromatic). The product is our target molecule which includes the heterocycle attached to aromatic ring via N? Actually our target SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1. This is a tertiary amine (piperazine?) attached to aromatic ring with nitro and O-bridge etc. The template suggests the aryl part is c:6 (the aromatic carbon attached to N). The amine nucleophile is [NH2]-[c:6] (an aniline). The leaving group is Cl attached to aromatic.

Thus precursors: 1) Cl-aryl (aryl chloride) with same substitution pattern as aromatic part of product (i.e., the aromatic ring with nitro and O-bridge). 2) Aniline (NH2 attached to same aromatic carbon). But the template also includes the heterocycle part? Actually the heterocycle is part of product side, not changed. So the heterocycle remains attached to N. So the precursors are: the aryl chloride (Cl attached to aromatic) and the amine (NH2 attached to aromatic). The heterocycle remains as part of product? Wait the product includes heterocycle attached to aromatic via N. In retro, we break that N-aryl bond, giving aryl chloride and aryl amine? Actually the product side is [c:6]-[N...] meaning aromatic carbon attached to N of heterocycle. The retro step breaks that bond, giving aryl chloride (Cl attached to aromatic) and NH2 attached to aromatic (aniline). The heterocycle remains as separate fragment? The template shows the heterocycle remains attached to N? Actually the product side includes the heterocycle attached to aromatic carbon. The reactants side includes Cl-aryl and NH2-aryl. So the heterocycle is not a separate precursor; it's part of the product side, so after retro, we get two fragments: the aryl chloride and the aryl amine. The heterocycle is not a separate precursor; it's part of the product (target). So the precursors list should be two SMILES: the aryl chloride and the aryl amine.

We need to apply the template to our target to get actual SMILES. Use apply_template with template ID? We have template hash but not ID. The reaction_id maybe corresponds to a template ID? Not sure. Could use apply_template with the retro_smarts_template directly? The tool apply_template expects template ID, not SMARTS. We might need to get template by ID. The search result didn't give template ID. Might be template_id is something like "template_1118219"? Not sure. Could try get_template with that ID.
Let's try get_template with reaction_id as string.
